summary: Corrected the two test defects T31 diagnosed and refused to touch, in the two named files only. Defect 1 (publication-claimability.test.ts:270): independently re-derived the pool timeline (start 20 -> alice's claim at step 5 leaves 19 -> step 6's top-up mints 1 replacement, confirmed against outbound.publicationPool.test.ts's B-7 assertion that `pool.claimable` reports live-members-after-top-up, i.e. back to 20 -> carol's step-7 claim leaves 19 for the step-8 raw-drain loop) and confirmed the implementer's suggested reading (N-1 = 19) is the only one consistent with the file's own step 6 and with B-7; the rejected reading (N-2 = 18, treating the two claims as if the step-6 top-up never happened) would falsify B-7 instead. Changed `LIMITS.PREKEY_MIN_COUNT - 2` to `LIMITS.PREKEY_MIN_COUNT - 1` and corrected the comment above it. Defect 2 (two-process.test.ts:168): imported LIMITS from @echolet/protocol and changed the publish-traffic filter's expected length from the literal 2 to `2 * LIMITS.PREKEY_MIN_COUNT`, derived rather than hardcoded. Searched the whole of apps/cli for other publish traffic counted through a filter/reduce/length shape rather than a direct assertion (`keryx ctx rg` for the route literal, for `.filter(...=>...path`, and for reduce/length-comparison patterns across test/e2e): found exactly four traffic.filter(...).toHaveLength(...) sites in two-process.test.ts (168 publish, 175 send, 177 claim, 185 ack) plus filter-based helpers in four other files keyed on /poll, /ack, /claim and /send - none of those other seven touch /v2/prekeys/publish, so none is affected by the pool multiplier; line 168 was the only site needing correction. Both target files pass in isolation on Node v26.5.0. Full CLI suite (`npx vitest run` in apps/cli): 272 passed, 1 failed of 273 - the failure is a THIRD, previously unflagged site (src/runtime/inbound.test.ts:324) that the pool also invalidates, reported below as F-001 and deliberately NOT fixed because it is a different class (a local one-time-prekey store snapshot equality, not publish-traffic counting) outside this dispatch's two-defect-plus-publish-count-search mandate; a follow-up task was spawned for it. Both cli.relayErrorCodes.test.ts and cli.senderQuota.test.ts (the CPU-contention class T31 flagged) passed in this full-suite run with no isolation re-run needed. Go: both `-count=1 -race` runs (tagged relayv2 and untagged) are all ok with zero data races, and the three named reservation-guard tests pass with all five/two subtests green, both guard test files byte-identical to T29's recorded digests. Workspace typecheck (`pnpm -r typecheck`) is clean across all 7 projects, confirming the new LIMITS import compiles. No product file, no documentation file and no file beyond the two named tests was changed. No store key, private key, plaintext or HTTP request body was printed or recorded.

findings.problem: A third, previously unflagged pre-existing assertion that the T31 pool implementation invalidates, of a different class from the two this dispatch was scoped to fix. `expect(await snapshot(alice, nativePrefixes)).toEqual(before)` expects that a send() which fails (via an injected persistence failure gated on the first transaction to touch `cli:outbox:` keys) leaves ALL native store state, including the `pre:` prefix, identical to `before` (captured right after `pair()`, before any publish, at which point only `pre:1` exists from identity creation). Measured: after the failed send, the store holds `pre:1` through `pre:20`. Root cause: the `send()` test helper (lines 49-81) calls `messenger.publish()` before `messenger.send()`; under T31's pool implementation, publish() durably mints the full N=20-member pool via mintPublicationSlot, which by design commits each member as its own transaction BEFORE it can be offered to anyone (t31-implementation-report.md section 1.1) - so the pool top-up is real, durable, deliberate state that is NOT part of the send's own atomic outbox-commit transaction and therefore is not rolled back by the injected failure.
findings.impact: Deterministic failure (reproduced twice: full suite and isolated `npx vitest run src/runtime/inbound.test.ts`), not the CPU-contention class T31's F-003 named. It sits outside this dispatch's mandate (the two named defects, plus only sites found by searching for indirect publish-TRAFFIC counting) because this assertion counts local one-time-prekey STORE state, not HTTP publish requests - it matched neither this session's filter/reduce/length search nor T29's F-001 or T31's F-002 enumerations, all of which were scoped to request counting. Fixing it here would exceed the explicit two-file change authorization.
findings.suggested_fix: Not attempted under this dispatch's scope. A follow-up task was spawned (mcp__ccd_session__spawn_task, task_7406ec35) with the full diagnosis: likely fixes are capturing `before` after a publish rather than before it, or asserting the outbox/history/session rollback property separately from the pre: prefix count, keeping any pool-size expectation derived from LIMITS.PREKEY_MIN_COUNT rather than a literal.
findings.evidence: `cd apps/cli && npx vitest run src/runtime/inbound.test.ts`: 1 failed, 10 passed. `AssertionError: expected { …(20) } to deeply equal { Object (pre:1) }` at inbound.test.ts:324, with the received object showing pre:1 through pre:20 and the expected object showing only pre:1. Reproduced identically inside the full-suite run (272 passed, 1 failed of 273).
